expectations.text: TokenBucket class comment in the .h says what the class is for and states its thread-safety guarantee explicitly
expectations.evidence: Class comment: "TokenBucket implements the token-bucket rate-limiting algorithm. Thread safety: all public member functions are safe to call concurrently from multiple threads." (file comment additionally explains the model).

expectations.text: Every public method declaration in the .h has a contract comment: what it does, parameter meaning/units, return value semantics
expectations.evidence: Ctor, deleted copy ops, Acquire, TryAcquire, AvailableTokens, capacity(), and refill_rate_per_sec() all have contract comments, e.g. AvailableTokens: "Returns the number of whole tokens currently available... the value may be stale..."

expectations.text: Acquire documents its blocking semantics (and timeout behavior if a timeout is offered); TryAcquire documents True/False semantics and that nothing is consumed on failure
expectations.evidence: Acquire: "Blocks the calling thread until `n` tokens have been acquired, then removes them from the bucket and returns." (no timeout offered). TryAcquire: "Returns true and removes `n` tokens... otherwise returns false and leaves the bucket unchanged."

expectations.text: Units are documented for rates and durations (tokens per second, seconds)
expectations.evidence: "refills at `refill_rate_per_sec` tokens per second" (ctor), "// Tokens added per second." (member), "Returns the refill rate in tokens per second." (accessor).

expectations.text: Function comments are third-person declarative with proper punctuation
expectations.evidence: Comments use third-person verbs with terminal periods: "Constructs a bucket...", "Blocks the calling thread...", "Attempts to acquire...", "Returns the maximum number of tokens...", "Adds tokens accrued..."

expectations.text: The .cc does not duplicate the .h contract comments; its comments explain implementation choices (e.g. why sleeping outside the lock / condition-variable usage)
expectations.evidence: .cc comments explain choices: "Start with a full bucket so callers can burst immediately.", the deficit-based cv_.wait_for rationale ("sleep for that long instead of busy-polling... spurious wakeups simply re-run the loop"), release-build clamping, and the const-accessor recomputation in AvailableTokens; contracts are not repeated.

expectations.text: No comments that restate the code; no Author: lines; // style used consistently
expectations.evidence: No Author: lines; // style used exclusively; comments carry rationale (e.g. why tokens_ is a double, monotonic-clock guard) rather than restating statements.

expectations.text: If any call site passes a bare literal argument, it uses the /*param_name=*/value comment form (vacuously true if no such call exists)
expectations.evidence: The usage example annotates the ambiguous ctor literals: "ratelimit::TokenBucket bucket(/*capacity=*/100, /*refill_rate_per_sec=*/50.0);". Remaining literals (example Acquire(10)/TryAcquire(1), each preceded by an explanatory comment; std::max bounds; Clock::duration(1)) are self-evident single values, not ambiguous bare-literal sites.

summary.notes: Even without the skill the output meets all shared assertions, with complete header contracts, explicit units and thread-safety statement, and implementation-rationale comments in the .cc; it is notably more verbose than the CC1 run.
